newsitem.title: INDIA: India SEBI panel to discuss derivatives - paper.
newsitem.headline: India SEBI panel to discuss derivatives - paper.

text.p: A committee on derivatives set up by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was scheduled to meet on Thursday to consider issues relating to options and futures trading, the Economic Times said.

The newspaper said on Thursday that the main item on the agenda of the meeting was to discuss whether mutual funds should be permitted into derivatives trading and to examine if the current legal framework allowed them to do so. India has not allowed futures and options trading yet, but SEBI, the stock market regulator, intends to do so after examining the issue in detail.
The newspaper said the expert committee, headed by L.C. Gupta, was expected to discuss whether derivatives trading needed a new exchange or the current stock exchanges were sufficient.
The panel was also considering the possibility of a centralised clearing house for derivatives trading, it said.
The committee would take a close look at the validity of stock market indices currently used in India and consider measures that may be required to set up a new index for derivatives, it said.
Another issue set for discussion is the qualifications needed for brokers trying to enter derivatives trade, it said.
The committee was expected by SEBI to submit a report within three months, but it may not be possible for it to do so, the newspaper said.

India's National Stock Exchange submitted a proposal to SEBI last year and had hoped to introduce futures and options by December, but SEBI decided to consider the pros and cons of introducing derivatives in the Indian market, it said.
